context: Sachiko and Goro recall their wedding day.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、過去の結婚式、覚えてる？
lines.en: Grandpa — do you remember that past wedding?
lines.style: Soft, meandering opening. Voice settles into a warm recall, unhurried. Slight lift on the question, genuinely curious if he remembers this the way she does. Tender but not fragile.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: Quiet certainty, no hesitation. Eyes far away—not lost, but definitely elsewhere. Three words that land with weight. Each image crystalline in his memory, delivered spare and perfect.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お父さんの着物、青、綺麗だった。
lines.en: Father's kimono was so blue. So beautiful.
lines.style: Voice grows softer, almost wondering. Pause before naming the color—she's seeing it again. Gentle, almost whispered admiration. The beauty still moves her after all these years.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: Your smile. I haven't forgotten it.
lines.style: Direct and steady. No performance, no elaboration needed. Speaks like this is fact, unchangeable as time. Slight roughness in the voice—age and honesty together. Simple devotion.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 一緒の時間、大切な思い出。
lines.en: Time spent together—those are the precious memories.
lines.style: Gentle closing wisdom, not a statement but a soft conclusion. Voice settles lower, reflective. The kind of simple truth an old person arrives at and finally speaks aloud.
